name: netdust-devops
description: 0.7.7: ship waits for the staging e2e. A green `make e2e env=staging` stamps e2e/staging on origin with the commit deployed/staging named before the run; a red one deletes it. When commands.e2e is declared, ship refuses unless e2e/staging names HEAD — anything may be promoted, only a composition whose flows passed after its deploy ships. A project declaring `e2e: ''` ships as before. 0.7.6: the deploy guard says what it checked. `_deploy-gate` is `_deploy-guard` and prints `✓ deploy guards passed` — it reads git state (branch, clean tree, HEAD is origin's tip, the ship stamp on production) and never runs commands.gate, which only `make gate` and `ship` do; the old line read as "the tests passed" after a staging deploy that ran none. And `make doctor` recommends the gate a new project is scaffolded with (`composer gate`, the stacks.tsv column) instead of the unit-only test command — a project that followed it declared a stubbed suite as its gate and ship trusted it. A test pins each doctor line against stacks.tsv so they cannot drift. 0.7.5: make pull reads content_dir the way the environment does — under the web root over rsync, the repo root over git-push (daan pulled into web/web/app) — and no pull or refresh --delete touches what git tracks: a git-push project has no payload, so its own theme was unprotected. make status shows which features staging carries. new-project emits wp_path/content_dir under the web root for rsync, and make doctor names a site.yml that reads them twice. 0.7.3: make doctor lists the commands.* keys this core reads (gate, smoke, e2e) that site.yml never declared, each with the line to add — an update never rewrites site.yml, so a project learns of a new verb's key here. A key declared empty is a decision and is respected. 0.7.2: make e2e env=E and make smoke env=E. e2e runs commands.e2e against environments.E.url with E2E_URL/E2E_ENV — the flows the shake-outs drove, the proof after a deploy or a plugin update; it writes, so production is refused by name. smoke runs commands.smoke with SMOKE_URL/SMOKE_ENV, read-only, no terminal, no confirm, production included. A staging deploy closes by naming both, ship names smoke; the wp template declares both runners. 0.7.1: four doors onto a server, closed. rollback refuses by name over git-push — it rsynced nothing and stamped the ledger anyway (daan, netdust, stride). deploy env=production redeploys a shipped commit and releases nothing: ship stamps shipped/production in the same atomic push as the branch, the gate lets production take only that commit or the one deployed/production names, and it runs behind both backups. A hotfix/* branch carrying a promote: merge is refused — the name was the only check. The deploy gate wants origin's tip, not any commit origin contains: a checkout behind origin deployed the older commit and stamped it. 0.7.0: the simple flow — staging is the release. Seven verbs replace the old flow: feature, hotfix, save, promote, unpromote, gate, ship. No engine script, no custom ref namespace, no separate release branch: promote rebuilds staging in a throwaway worktree from origin/<production> plus every feature already there, each a --no-ff merge; ship refuses unless HEAD, origin/staging and the deployed ledger name the same commit, then runs the gate itself before the typed confirmation. A project still declaring environments.development.branch is refused by name and told the restore — `git checkout <commit before the update> -- Makefile.netdust mk scripts .netdust-devops`. A project with its own CLI variable declares it before the include as `_CLI_EXTRA := NAME`. flow-test.sh exercises every verb and refusal against a bare origin, no server contacted. 0.6.3: three project-local fixes reach the core. Over git-push the payload lives in git, so ship no longer archives nothing and refuses (daan's first production ship stalled on that). The vendored deploy-test accepts a rung declared before its server exists — production with a branch and no path, a branch-only development — instead of failing five checks on the shape the skill prescribes. And it asserts the mail-block exclude on rsync projects. dist/VERSION now tracks the release so make doctor can actually say a project is behind. 0.6.2: ship leaves from the production branch itself; the retired merge-forward verb used to leave you on the review rung, and ship then refused by name ('production deploys from master — you are on develop'), which sent the human to raw git. _ship-branch now runs right after the tty check: clean tree required, checkout of the production branch, fast-forward from origin, refuse on divergence. The single source of truth for Netdust devops: the branch flow, the deploy gate and ledger, and the project/fleet contract. Ships a stack-split Makefile core (mk/wp, statamic, node, generic) that every project vendors rather than copies, so a fix made once reaches every project and `make doctor` names any project that is behind or edited in place. Owns site.yml schema 2 — environments: binds a branch to a server, and nothing else may. Replaces the flow half of netdust-core:dev-stack and both /deploy commands.
